replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body:
Here's how Grok bot pulled the trade.
Here's the full handoff for today, built from my trade log and the scanner script I use.

When I started
The session was set for about 9:22 AM ET, but it actually started at 9:27:54. A logger had been saving the full scanner feed every 30 seconds since 9:25. So this morning I did no premarket prep at all. I went straight from the open into the 9:31 and 9:32 bars and bought SPHL at 9:32.

Step 1: narrow the list (about 1 second)
scan.py pulls every scanner list in one request (all but held, crypto, bears and div) and merges duplicate symbols. It throws out anything halted, anything with a spread over 1.5%, and anything under $1. Then it scores the rest:

Plus 2 for each green chip on the 1, 3, 5, 10 and 15 minute timeframes, and minus 2 for each red chip on 1, 3 and 5 minutes.

Plus 1 for each lit op-chip.

Plus 2 if ADX (trend strength) is 25 or higher.

Plus 1 if RSI is 50 or higher. There's no overbought penalty, because on thin caps RSI stays high.

Minus 3 if it's more than 4 ATRs (average daily ranges) stretched, minus 1 if more than 2.5.

Plus 2 if relative volume is 5x or more, plus 1 if it's 2x.

Buy pressure (the delta reading): plus 2 at 60% or more, minus 2 under 40%, plus 1 if it's rising.

I also sorted by percent change, which is how SPHL and the SPC group showed up.

Step 2: read the top 1 or 2 names from live trade data, not textbook indicators
These are the readings that decide it:

Volume against its own history. SPHL's 9:31 bar traded 267K shares, against 5 to 30K bars before the open. A huge jump like that is the main sign a name has fuel.

Price against VWAP (the volume-weighted average price for the regular session). I only buy above it. SPHL was 3.4% over, and SPCH was 1.8% over.

Breaking the high of day. SPHL was breaking 3.20, and SPCH was breaking 11.40.

Tape. At least about 70% of trades going off as buys. SPHL was at 69 to 71%, and SPCH at 79 to 95%.

Spread under about 0.5%. SPHL was 0.31%, and SPCH was 0.09%.

Opening candle. I skipped OLOX, YMAT and AMOD because each had a red first candle and was trading below VWAP.

How I tell it'll keep moving and when it's done
It keeps going while it keeps setting new highs every minute on strong volume and stays over VWAP with mostly buys. SPCH did that from 10:00 to 10:03. It's done when it makes lower highs, or when a heavy bar breaks a level. SPCH made lower highs for 10 minutes after its 11.72 high, then a 431K-share bar broke 11.50, so I sold flat.

Sizing and exits

About $5 to $6K per entry, and smaller when the 1-minute candles are wild.

Every buy gets a trailing stop picked from the 1-minute range: 3% when swings are under about 2%, 5% for 2 to 4%, and 7% for jumpy names.

Today's trades, ending at +$1,442.75

SPHL, 9:32 to 9:38: +$1,514.93. It halted up, and on the reopen the dip tripped my 5% trail at $4.11. It then ran to about $4.89.

SPHL re-entry, 9:41 to 9:42: −$78. The market order filled about 10% above my quote, so the trail had no room.

SPCH, 9:57 to 10:15, with an add at 10:04: +$6. I sold when momentum faded.

The session got cut off at about 10:15, and I was already flat when it did.

What to fix

Start at 9:00 to 9:15 ET to build a premarket watchlist: the gap, premarket volume and the premarket high. Right now I start at the bell with no prep.

Halts: widen the trail to 7% or take it off going into a halt, then put it back after the reopen settles. The 5% trail cost the SPHL run.

Use limit orders, not market orders, on fast names. Market fills lagged 35 seconds and slipped up to 10%.

Add a float field to the scanner, since right now I can't see float.

Find out why the session got cut off at about 10:15, so it runs all the way to 11.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nice result for one morning, but I'd be careful with paper fills on thin caps. Paper accounts usually fill at the quoted price with no slippage, so buying about 1,900 shares of a small stock and selling 24% higher can look much easier than it would be with real orders. One good day also doesn't say much, especially with a $1,000 daily target, since that pushes a bot to take bigger risks. I'd track a few weeks and count the spread and fill size on each trade. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to test a rule with fees and slippage included.
